transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope it's okay that I'm here. I just... I've been having a little bit of trouble lately, and I wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in. 

I guess what brings me in is... well, I've gotten into this habit, and it's kind of embarrassing to admit, but I keep making myself throw up after I eat. It's not all the time, just... sometimes I have to do it in the bathroom at the dry cleaners where I work, or right when I get home. I know it sounds bad, but it's just... I hate that it's started feeling like the only way I can calm down, you know? Does that make sense? I really want to fix it, I promise.
Can you tell me more about the times when you make yourself vomit—do you usually eat a large amount of food right before that, or is it more like regular meals or snacks?

Um... well, I really try to just eat normal portions, I promise I do. But... I guess when it happens, it's usually after I've eaten a lot more than I meant to. I hope it's okay to be honest about this, it's just really embarrassing to say out loud. 

When I get like that, I just kind of... lose track. I can go through a full bag of chips, and then maybe some pastries I picked up from the corner store near work, and whatever leftovers are around, plus some sweet drinks. Just all in one sitting. It's like I don't even really notice how much is actually gone until I'm looking at the wrappers. I know that probably sounds terrible, doesn't it? I really am trying to be better about it, I swear.
When you're eating all of that in one sitting, do you feel like you can't control how much you're eating, or that you can't stop eating once you start?

I... um... I hope you don't think I'm just weak or greedy, because I really do try to be good, I swear. But... yeah, I guess that's exactly it. 

Once I start, it's like... it feels like my hands just keep reaching for the next thing, even while I'm literally telling myself in my head to stop. It's so weird, it's almost like I'm just watching myself do it, and I just can't make myself quit. I know I should be able to just put the food away, and I'm really trying to work on having better willpower, I promise. Is it okay that I feel that way? I just don't want you to think I'm not trying.

Do these episodes of eating a lot and making yourself vomit happen at least once a week, and have they been affecting your life in ways that feel hard to manage, like making it hard to focus at work or feel okay around other people?

I... I really hope you're not too disappointed in me, because I know I should be handling things better. But... yes, I guess it is at least once a week. Honestly, for a few months now, most weeks I end up having at least a couple of those times where I eat way more than I meant to. 

And then I just... I try to fix it, or undo it, I guess. Sometimes by throwing up, like I said, or... or sometimes I'll just try to fast and not eat anything at all the next day, or I'll try to exercise a lot to work it off. I just want to make it right after I mess up, you know? 

And as for work... I mean, I always make sure I get my work done at the dry cleaners, I promise I do! I don't want to be a bad employee. But it does make it a little hard to focus sometimes, or feel normal around the customers and my coworkers, because I'm just so worried they can tell what I've been doing. I hope it's okay that I'm telling you all this... am I answering your questions okay?
Can you tell me specifically how often these episodes of eating a lot and then trying to undo it happen in a typical week?

Um... well, I know I just mentioned it, and I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much or being confusing... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. 

But, um, I guess if I really think about a typical week... for the past few months, it's usually at least two times a week. Sometimes maybe a little more, but I really try to keep it from getting out of hand, I promise. It's just... yeah, a couple of times a week I end up having one of those times where I eat too much, and then I have to... you know, fix it. By throwing up, or just not eating the next day, or going for a really long run to try and sweat it out. 

Is that what you needed to know? I hope I'm explaining it okay... I just really want to be helpful and do this right.
Do these episodes or the thoughts around them make it hard for you to feel good about yourself or cause you a lot of worry, even when you’re not in the middle of one?

Um... yeah, they do. I really hope you don't think I'm just letting my whole life fall apart, because I try so hard to keep everything looking normal, I promise. But... the worry is kind of always there. 

It feels like my whole day just gets arranged around hiding what happened. I don't want anyone to know and think less of me. So I end up... well, I've skipped out on after-work meals with people, and sometimes I catch myself rushing through my errands, or even rushing through my tasks at the dry cleaners... just because my brain is so preoccupied with figuring out how I'm going to make up for eating. 

I try really hard to push those thoughts away so I can do a good job, I swear I do. I never want to let anyone down. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too crazy... I just want to be honest with you so I can do this right.

Can you tell me if you have experienced any episodes in the past three months where you felt you had completely lost control over your eating, followed by making yourself vomit or engaging in other behaviors like fasting or excessive exercise to prevent weight gain?

I... I know we sort of just talked about this, and I really, really hope I'm not frustrating you by repeating myself. I want to make sure I'm answering you the right way. 

But, um, yes. For a few months now, it's been happening. Like I said, most weeks I'll have at least a couple of those times where I... I just eat way more than I meant to, and I feel like I can't stop. And then I get so scared about gaining weight or ruining everything, so I have to try and undo it. 

I'll make myself throw up, or I'll just promise myself I won't eat anything the whole next day, or I'll go work out as hard as I can to burn it off. I just... I try to fix it so it doesn't leave a mark, you know? I hope that's what you were asking... am I giving you the right details?
Do you judge yourself harshly based on your body shape or weight, even when other people might not see anything wrong?

Um... yes. I mean, I try not to let it get in the way, I really do. I want to be a good worker and a good person, but... it's just really hard. 

I can be having a perfectly fine day, doing good at the shop, getting all the orders right, but... if I catch my reflection in the glass window and my stomach or my hips look big to me... it just ruins everything. I instantly feel like a complete failure. Even if a customer just told me I did a great job with their coats, all I can think about is how awful my body looks. 

I know other people probably don't even notice, and I really hope you don't think I'm just being vain or silly. I just... I can't help but judge myself so, so harshly if I feel like I'm taking up too much space or looking the wrong way. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too shallow... I just want to make sure I'm answering you right.
Do you feel that your overall sense of self-worth is strongly connected to your body shape or weight?

Um, yes, I think so. I know I sort of just mentioned this, and I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much or wasting your time... I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need. 

But, yeah, it really is tied to everything for me. Like I was saying about the shop... I can be having a great day, getting all the dry cleaning done perfectly, making the customers happy... but if I happen to catch my reflection in the window and my stomach or my hips look big to me, it's like all that good stuff just vanishes. I just instantly feel like a complete failure as a person. 

It doesn't matter how hard I work, if my body isn't right, I just feel like I'm not worth anything. I try to hide it, I swear I do, because I don't want anyone to think I'm doing a bad job or that I'm ungrateful. I just... I hope you understand what I mean? Am I explaining it okay?
Do you find that your overall happiness or sense of being okay with yourself depends mostly on how your body looks or how much you weigh?

Um, yeah, I guess it does. I mean, I know we literally just talked about that, and I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm just saying the same thing over and over. I really hope you aren't getting annoyed with me. 

But, yes, it's like... if I step on the scale in the morning and the number is higher than I want it to be, or if my work uniform feels even a tiny bit tight, my whole day is just ruined. I can't be happy. I just feel awful about myself, no matter what else happens. 

I know it probably sounds really silly to let something like that control my mood so much, and I try so hard to just put on a smile and be cheerful for everyone else. I just... I don't know how to separate the two things. Is that... is that the kind of answer you were looking for? I hope I'm being helpful.
Can you tell me how often, on average, you make yourself vomit or engage in other behaviors like fasting or excessive exercise in a typical week?

Um... oh, wow, um... I guess... I mean, I really don't want you to think I'm doing this all the time, or that I'm completely out of control, because I'm not. I still go to work every day and do a good job. 

But... well, for months now, I guess most weeks... there are at least a couple of times where I just... I end up eating way more than I meant to. And then I just feel so awful and guilty, and I know I have to fix it. So I'll try to undo it by throwing up, or maybe I just won't eat anything the next day, or I'll try to exercise a lot to burn it off. 

It's usually just a couple of times a week, though. I really try to keep it under control. I know it's not the best thing to do, and I'm a little embarrassed to even admit it... I hope you don't think less of me for it. I just panic when I feel like I've ruined everything. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
